Bead description mentioned 12 fields including i_non_self_issued and max_path_len; in reality i_non_self_issued is computed inline via is_self_issued_cert(cert) and max_path_len lives on ValidationPolicy (already accessible), so the struct has 10 fields. description:
## Why

`chain_walk` carries 7+ mutable state vars (working_spki, working_issuer_name, working_issuer_is_san_identity, valid_policy_tree, permitted_subtrees, excluded_subtrees, max_path_len, i_non_self_issued, explicit_policy, policy_mapping, inhibit_any_policy, nc_constrained_types) through the loop body. The high-risk helpers (H8/H9/H10/H11) need these vars; threading them as individual params would make the function signatures fragile. The PKIX-als9 description explicitly recommends a struct.

## What

Introduce `pub(crate) struct WorkingState { ... }` in pkix-path/src/lib.rs collecting the policy/NC/path-len state. Doc-comment each field with its RFC 5280 §6.1 origin. `chain_walk` constructs it once at §6.1.2 init (lines 2042–2111), mutates fields in the loop, and consumes it at §6.1.5 final wrap-up. No helper extraction yet — purely a state-grouping refactor.

## Sequencing

Lands BEFORE H8 (first helper that needs the struct). H1–H7 do not need WorkingState; they take individual params.

## Acceptance

- New struct `WorkingState` defined and used in chain_walk.
- All existing PKITS tests pass: `cargo test -p pkix-path`.
- `cargo clippy --all-features -p pkix-path -- -D warnings` clean.
- Doc-comment on the struct names each field s RFC 5280 §6.1 source.
- No behaviour change.
title: als9: prep — introduce WorkingState struct (groups policy/NC/path-len state)
